text:
Marathon's stock ticked up slightly today after a remarkable two-week rally, riding a wave driven by rising oil prices and geopolitical tension in the Middle East. U.S. crude has climbed sharply as Iran escalates attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, with Brent crude touching $110 this week — higher oil prices improve refiner margins (the difference between what they pay for crude and what they sell refined products for). Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity, so the industry is well-positioned to convert that pricier crude into fuel sales, which benefits Marathon's bottom line.

The broader context amplifies this: physical oil delivery costs have surged due to elevated tanker rates, which means the "real" economic value of crude is even higher than the headline price suggests. Combined with ongoing geopolitical risk (Iran's threats of further escalation) keeping markets nervous and supportive of higher oil prices, refiners are operating in an unusually favorable environment — though that premium could be fleeting if tensions ease or shipping normalizes.
